chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Proof of God upon the servants is the Prophet, and the Proof between the servants and God is the intellect.

key_terms.العباد: Al-'ibad — the servants; all human beings as servants (slaves) of God
key_terms.العقل: 'Aql — the intellect or reason; in Shia theology, a foundational source of religious knowledge alongside revelation
key_terms.النبي: Al-Nabi — the Prophet; here referring to the Prophet Muhammad (saww) as the external divine proof upon all humanity
key_terms.حجة: Hujja — divine proof or argument; a technical theological term denoting God's established authority and the basis of accountability

ai.seo_question: What is the proof (hujja) of God upon His servants according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates a theological distinction between two types of divine proof (hujja): externally, God's proof upon humanity is the Prophet (saww), who delivers revelation and guidance; internally, the proof between each individual servant and God is the intellect ('aql), which enables moral discernment and accountability. This hadith reflects the Shia theological tradition's elevation of reason as a foundational source of religious obligation, parallel to prophetic authority, and explains why those deprived of reason are not held legally accountable.
